# Daddarajātaka (Ja 304)

**ID:** Ja 304
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Daddarajātaka* (Ja 304) is a canonical birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection (PTS volume III, pp. 15–17) [Fausböll 1883; Hazra 1994]. According to the narrative framework, the Buddha relates the story while dwelling at Jetavana concerning a short-tempered or choleric monk (*kodhana bhikkhu*) [Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897]. In the past story, during the reign of Brahmadatta at Benares, the Bodhisatta was born as Mahādaddara, the elder son of King Sūradaddara of the Daddara nāgas, who lived at the foot of Mount Daddara in the Himalayan region [Fausböll 1883; Fausböll 1897; Cowell 1897]. When his younger brother Culladaddara was sentenced to banishment for violently abusing the nāga maidens, Mahādaddara accompanied him into a three-year exile on a human dunghill (*ukkārabhūmi*), where the two nāga princes had to endure harassment from villagers without retaliation [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897].

The jātaka's verses emphasize patience, restraint, and forbearance when living among strangers, counseling one to build a great storehouse to store away harsh insults (*mahantaṁ koṭṭhaṁ kay'rātha duruttānaṁ nidhetave*) and noting that one should not reside among unknown folk without understanding their manners and customs (*vinaya*) [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1883; Hazra 1994]. In the identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the hot-tempered brother Culladaddara is identified with the choleric monk, while Mahādaddara is identified as the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1883].

DharmaNexus identifies extensive text reuse of the verses (§2.1–4.4) within the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* and records that segments §3.1–4.4 are reused in the Pali anthology *Mahārahanīti* (§1229–1237) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns verses from this jātaka with the Tibetan *Nāgarājābherīgāthā* (D0325, ཀླུའི་རྒྱལ་པོ་རྔ་སྒྲའི་ཚིགས་སུ་བཅད་པ།) [DharmaNexus].
